name: Santa María la Blanca

position.source: https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/150415814 (centroid of the outline; long axis at 73.8°, the foot of the naves faces west-south-west)

rights.note: Main synagogue of Toledo, about 1180 (date on a beam; rebuilt in the 13th century), Mudéjar work of anonymous Muslim builders for the Jewish community led by Yosef ben Shoshan; church from 1411; chapels at the head by Alonso de Covarrubias (16th century). Owned by the Archdiocese of Toledo, open as a monument.

notes: Built by code (model_sources/Q1568115_santa_maria_la_blanca.py, tools/meshkit.py) with AI assistance. The five naves step up to the central one: lean-to tiled roofs over the outer and inner naves and a gable roof over the central nave, small clerestory windows where the raised naves stand above the lower roofs; whitewashed walls on a brick plinth, the door with its glazed transom and the big modern grid windows in the foot. The heights are estimated on oblique photos (±10 %); the chapels of Covarrubias at the head are kept inside the volumes of the naves. The garden courtyard in front of the foot and along the north side is included: sand floor a step below the door, paved path, low brick beds, the cypresses and two broadleaf trees (positions from the orthophoto, ±2 m), the wall round it and the gate with its steps down to the street. The interior (pillars and arches) is not modelled.
